description.narrative:
The three overarching objectives of the Women Deliver 2023 conference are:
a) Holding leaders accountable
b) Catalyzing collective action
c) Reframing "who leads"

Women Deliver 2023 is the world's largest conference on gender equality and SRHR and will be held in Kigali, Rwanda, 17-20 July 2023. Women Deliver 2023 has three overarching goals - all linked to gender equality and SRHR: a) holding leaders accountable b) catalyze joint action and c) to redefine "who leads". WD 2023 is the sixth global conference, and the second held in the global south. WD2023 is relevant based on the global gender equality strategy and several other Swedish strategies that have a focus on SRHR. The conference is considered to contribute positively to the overall goals for Generation Equality Forum (GEF).

Women Deliver 2023 är världens största konferens om jämställdhet och SRHR och hålls i Kigali, Rwanda, 17- ­20 juli 2023. Women Deliver 2023 har tre övergripande mål - alla kopplade till jämställdhet och SRHR: a) att hålla ledare till svars b) katalysera gemensamt agerande samt c) att omdefiniera "vem som leder". WD 2023 är den sjätte i ordningen, och den andra konferensen som hålls i det globala syd. WD2023 är relevant utifrån den globala jämställdhetsstrategin och flera andra svenska strategier som har fokus på SRHR och betraktas bidra positivt till de övergripande målen för Generation Equality Forum (GEF).

The Women Deliver conference, held in Kigali Rwanda 17-23 July 2023, had over 6,300 participants from 170 countries. Another 10,000 participated online. This makes the conference one of the world's largest gatherings on gender equality. Sida's support to Women Deliver was a project grant to be specifically used for activities relating to the conference.
Both conference participants and an external evaluation gave testimonies of a successful conference that generated political and financial committments, was inclusive and fostered dynamic discussions amongst the participants and beyond. Some of the key results of the conference:
Objective 1: Hold leaders accountable
Financial commitments
- The Ministerial Forum, organised by the Ministry of Gender and Family Promotion in Rwanda, convened 24 ministers from multiple countries to discuss pressing themes such as digital technology and innovation, GBV prevention and response and women's economic justice.
- UNFPA and the European Parliamentarian Forum for Sexual and Reproductive Rights hosted the Parliamentarian Forum, gathering 48 parliamentarians from across the globe.
- Canada announced more than $200 million CAD in new funding via the SheSOARS initiative to support neglected and underfunded areas of SRHR, including family planning, comprehensive sexuality education (CSE), advocacy for SRHR, safe abortion and post-abortion care, and GBV.
- The Global Fund to Fight AIDS, TB, and Malaria, along with GSK and ViiV Healthcare, announced a three-year partnership (accompanied by USD $7.5 million in funding) for advancing gender equality in Africa.
- Open Society Foundation announced a new funding facility to counter anti-rights movements and provide investment for the most neglected SRH areas.
Political commitments
- The Rwandan Ministry of Health committed to decentralizing abortion care to midwives at the WD2023 Maternal Health Pre-Conference.
- African Women Rights Advocates (AWRA) and the Orchid Project introduced the Africa Network to End FGM/C. This is a first-of-its-kind, African-led, initiative aimed at advocating, lobbying, and connecting individuals and organizations working to end FGM/C in Africa.
- The "Kigali Call to Action: United for Women and Girl's Bodily autonomy" was announced by UNFPA to accelerate investments and actions, with women-led organizations and the feminist movement at its center.
Objective 2: Catalyze collective action
A key objective was supporting networking and fostering new partnerships. According to the post conference survey, 86% of participants made new connections at WD2023 which they deemed as "useful for ongoing initiatives". The participation and representation of participants from low income countries was a priority, leading to 68% of plenary speakers coming from ODA-eligible countries.
- Moreover, Women Deliver accredited over 240 media and content creators from 38 countries. The conference had 33 million impressions on social media and generated over 1,300 earned media mentions, representing a $15M advertising value equivalent. 40 scholarships were awarded to emerging journalists and content creators.
Objective 3: Re-frame who leads
Several efforts were taken to amplify diverse perspectives and voices during the WD 2023. This included scholarships to 232 young leaders and 18 young artists from ODA countries to enable their participation at the conference. All official WD 2023 sessions had at least one young person as a speaker. Throughout the planning process, Women Deliver implemented all agreed-upon accessibility measures and best practices to ensure best possible accessibility for participants.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
